strengths: Novel problem formulation identifying physics inconsistency in existing V2A models; well-motivated and intuitive
Technically sound architecture with careful design choices: VLM + 3D reconstruction for physics estimation, principled ∆-modulation for gradual injection
Comprehensive multi-dimensional evaluation: distribution matching, quality, semantic/temporal alignment, and novel APCC metric for physical plausibility
Convincing empirical results: lowest APCC-∆ (0.378 vs 0.536 for next-best), competitive across all other metrics, persuasive qualitative spectrograms
Well-designed ablation studies (Table 3) demonstrating physics conditioning drives improvements, not just additional training
Introduction of VGG-Impact benchmark and APCC metric addresses overlooked evaluation dimension; shows existing models have high APCC-∆ >0.5
User study across four aspects; clear improvements on physical plausibility dimension
weaknesses: Physics parameter estimation largely unvalidated: mass claims 'comparable to specialized expert models' without quantitative error metrics or ground truth; velocity depends on 3D reconstruction errors not characterized

Narrow evaluation scope: VGG-Impact has only 272 impact moments from 10 classes; APCC metric only measures onset strength correlation, ignores materials/damping/contact geometry; no human validation that APCC correlates with perceived plausibility

Incomplete physical model: only considers kinetic energy (mass/velocity); ignores material properties, friction, elasticity affecting impacts; no ablation showing individual component contributions (materials vs mass vs velocity)

Experimental design issues: two-stage training makes isolating physics conditioning gains difficult; compares PAVAS (44.1kHz) against 16kHz baselines, biasing sample rate comparisons; physics token dropout p=0.1 unjustified
Limited to impact sounds only: applicability to continuous sounds, friction, liquids, or multi-object scenarios unvalidated; method may not generalize beyond momentary interactions
Insufficient statistical rigor: user study with only 15 participants; no significance testing (t-tests) despite reporting standard deviations

Reproducibility concerns: exact versions of pretrained models (Qwen2.5-VL, Florence-2, SAM-2, CUT3R) not specified; VGG-Impact curation protocol insufficiently detailed; no code release mentioned; computational cost not reported
Missing error analysis: no characterization of physics estimation failures (occlusions, fast motion); no examples of still-implausible generated audio; ground-truth APCC computation unclear

strengths: Well-motivated problem identification addressing a genuine gap: current V2A models fail to enforce physical consistency (e.g., mass-loudness correlation)
Principled Δ-modulation design for injecting physics cues, empirically validated to outperform direct summation (Table 3)
Comprehensive experimental validation: comparisons against 9 baselines, thorough ablations, user study with 27 participants across 4 dimensions, robustness analyses
Novel benchmark (VGG-Impact) and metric (APCC) with robustness validation (inter-class shuffling 0.378→0.655; noise sensitivity analysis)
Physics estimation quality: mass ADE=6.954 (better than NeRF2Physics 8.730) with single-view input; velocity estimation outperforms SpatialVLM
Extensive supplementary material with implementation details, runtime profiling, missing-observation statistics, and generalization tests
Clear presentation of system architecture and thorough qualitative analysis via spectrograms showing improved temporal/spectral alignment
weaknesses: Limited novelty in individual components: primarily combines existing models (Qwen VLM, Florence-2, SAM2, CUT3R, MMAudio); Phy-Adapter is standard FiLM + residual conditioning applied to AdaLN
Narrow physics grounding despite title: only mass and velocity estimated (ignores material, elasticity, friction); no validation that generated audio obeys physics laws compared to simulators

APCC metric relies on oversimplified acoustic model (kinetic energy ∝ spectral onset strength) without empirical validation of linearity; doesn't account for material damping, frequency-dependent radiation, or contact geometry
VGG-Impact benchmark is small (272 impact moments, 10 classes) with subjective manual curation, limiting generalizability of physics evaluation claims
High missing observation rate: 65.15% of frames use SAM2 occlusion tokens; no analysis of performance degradation in heavily occluded scenarios
Prohibitive computational cost: 7.16s per 10-second video (Table S5), primarily from CUT3R (4.82s), making real-time/interactive applications impractical
Incremental improvements over MMAudio baseline: marginal gains in IS (17.51 vs 17.40), DeSync (0.446 vs 0.442), with main improvements in FD metrics and newly-proposed APCC metric
Limited generalization: Table S6 shows PAVAS performs worse on non-impact scenes in some metrics (FD_VGG: 1.09 vs 1.01); unclear scalability to other physics-dependent sounds

Two-stage training introduces potential train-test mismatch; backbone trained on diverse data then fine-tuned only on VGGSound; physics tokens dropout (p=0.1) during training may not reflect test conditions

Overclaiming physics consistency: comparison to specialized models [6, 85] uses different experimental setups (single-view vs multi-view); no actual validation against physics simulators or ground-truth physical laws
